Two places where the claim overstates what the numbers certify: (1) the class-sup widths are computed with sigma^2 <= r(1-r)/8, which is the UNCLIPPED arm variance; the class {|g|<=1} (and its maximiser g=1-8r+8r^2, |g|=1 at r=0,1) forces clipping of q_+- for every r, under which sigma^2 can exceed r(1-r)/8 (e.g. r=0.1, g=1: 0.0150 > 0.01125) and E[y|r] != g(r); with the clipping-valid bound 1/32 the sups become 0.1785/0.2490/0.1308 (9-13% larger), so the quoted sups are not upper bounds for the physical model the production simulation runs. (2) The m-budget table marks only narrow m=32 as a known first-order false positive, but at n=200 (4000 reps, clipped Bernoulli arms) the half-var m=128 cell (w_1=0.143<=0.15) has realised median HC1 width 0.183, q90 0.85, P(width<=0.15)=0.28 and 11% non-PD; the realised median falls below 0.15 only at m~192 (0.145) and q90 only near m=256; narrow m=64 (class c2 cell) similarly: median 0.162, 20% non-PD. The does-not-claim covers finite-sample behaviour generically, but the table as presented singles out one false positive. Minor nits: the unclipped sigma^2 = [2r(1-r)-g^2/2]/16 is negative for r<0.0076 (negligible mass; Gaussian-noise simulation of the stated model fails in the wide world); the parenthetical 'A1 bound min(m,4p)=8' is not what the formula needs -- at m=4 the centring term in V_44 = r^4 - r^8 still requires the 8th per-type moment, so the needed order is 8 for every m>=4, not min(m,8). The core proved statement stands; the quoted numbers are reproduced.
